read_me: docs/platform_specs.md. Every value says how well it is known: official (a platform's own developer or help page, read on verified_on), measured (measured by this project on the real account or files), third_party (blogs and vendor guides, which contradict each other), unresolved. Enforce official and measured values; treat the rest as advice and never as a fact. Meta's own preflight lives in config/meta_publishing.json and app/meta_publishing/validator.py; the encode targets of our clips (GOP, loudness, true peak) live in config/parameters/short_clips.json (short_clips.video.delivery).

video.notes: A reel published as a Page story cannot exceed 60 seconds. Error 1363040: the aspect ratio must lie between 16:9 and 9:16.

cover.how: A separate Graph API call (POST /{video}/thumbnails). It needs pages_read_user_content and pages_manage_engagement, which the current token lacks. A posted thumbnail cannot be changed or deleted through the API. GET /{video}/thumbnails works on drafts.

video.notes: The Instagram content-publishing page that could be read has no numbers; Meta's Reels guide above is used for both. Reels are published as a container with media_type=REELS and, for large files, a resumable upload to rupload.facebook.com.
video.rules_official: MOV or MP4, no edit lists, moov atom at the front, AAC at most 48 kHz mono or stereo, HEVC or H.264 progressive with a closed GOP, 4:2:0, 23-60 fps, at most 1920 px wide, VBR up to 25 Mbps, 3 s to 15 min, 300 MB (source: ig-user/media reference)

cover.advice: Sources contradict each other and none is official. The newest and most repeated claim is a 3:4 profile grid. A 1080x1080 centre square survives every candidate. Check the grid preview in the Instagram app on the real account before relying on any crop.
cover.how: Official (Graph API reference, ig-user/media, read 2026-11-17): `thumb_offset` = the frame in milliseconds used as the cover; `cover_url` (a public JPEG URL, 8 MB, sRGB, 9:16 recommended, otherwise cropped to the middle 9:16) is the cover for the Reels tab. Measured 2026-11-17 on the real account: a delivery copy that opens with the cover (thumb_offset 0) became the Reel's thumbnail. The profile grid crop stays unresolved.

video.notes: Every creator can post 3 minutes; some can post 5 or 10. 1080x1920 is the common size in the guides, not in the API page.

cover.how: No custom-image cover option was found in the Content Posting API page; TikTok takes a frame of the video. So the frame that should act as the cover has to be in the video itself. A guide says the thumbnail rarely decides a view from the For You feed and matters most on the profile grid and in search.

video.notes: Vertical videos up to 3 minutes; 'maximum resolution 1080p' is the short side, so 1080x1920 is allowed. The help page does not state an aspect ratio.

cover.advice: Blogs say a custom thumbnail on a Short may be limited to some accounts and that text should stay out of the top and bottom 15 percent; both are unverified. Test on the real channel.
cover.measured_2026-11-18: thumbnails.set worked on a Short of the real Persian channel: YouTube's `shortsAspectRatio` thumbnail (1080x1920) of the video is the reel cover. A link to the film in the description is accepted by videos.insert; whether it is clickable in the Shorts feed is unverified (the supported route is the related-video field set by hand in Studio).

cover_use.reel: The only upload candidate: Facebook Reels, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and the first frames of the TikTok video. Platforms take one cover per video.
cover_use.feed: A preview, and the picture for a Facebook or Instagram feed post. No source says a platform takes 4:5 as a reel cover.
cover_use.grid: A preview of a square profile grid. No source says a platform takes 1:1 as a reel cover.

audit_2026_11_17.scope: 49 finished clip files of case 15 (8 languages, clips C1 to C5, and some music variants)

found.gop_seconds: up to 8.3 (the encoder had no GOP setting, so x264 used 250 frames); Meta asks for 2 to 5
found.true_peak_db: at or above 0 in almost every clip (limiter at 0.95 and an AAC encode on top)
found.opening: the host is small in a wide studio shot for the first 3 seconds and the first frame carries no title

audit_2026_11_17.fixed: short_clips.video.delivery (a 2 s closed GOP, -14 LUFS, a -2 dB true-peak target, a -1 dB ceiling) is used by every new clip; delivery copies of the C1 clips of 8 languages were made beside the originals (delivery_C1.mp4). The originals are never replaced.
not_done: a closer host crop for the first seconds
a title frame at the very start of the video
caption wrapping of long Persian lines over a photo

creative_rules.rule: Open with one concrete, striking fact of the case in the first 2 to 3 seconds; never with an introduction such as 'today I want to talk about a case'.
Burn the captions in; many people watch without sound, so the caption is often the real hook. Highlight word by word.
One case per video; hook, context, escalation, turn, then the answer or an open question that invites comments.
Judge a hook by the early-retention curve of the platform's own analytics, not by taste; post different openers and compare.
Keep text, faces and logos inside the middle of the picture so that any crop and any platform overlay leaves them visible.

open_questions: Which crop does the Instagram profile grid use on the real account (3:4, 4:5 or 1:1)?
Can the real YouTube channel set a custom thumbnail on a Short?
Does the TikTok Content Posting API take a cover timestamp or image?
What do the largest true-crime channels do in their first seconds? No source with real data was found; it needs their videos or an analytics tool.
